headline.purpose: The page title at the top of every article header.

title.purpose: Section headings inside a detail card.

frame.purpose: Movie titles in a frame gutter and index entries; clamped to two lines.

fine.purpose: Uppercase mono button and chip labels.

label.purpose: Accession codes, years, rating figures, tabs and section labels; tabular mono, uppercase.

motion.name: step
motion.purpose: The only transition duration in the system; drops to 1ms under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: step-fn
motion.purpose: The only timing function. No easing curve exists anywhere in the project.

motion.name: mark-draw
motion.purpose: The chinagraph stroke drawing itself; the single declared exception to the step grammar.

motion.name: advance
motion.value: translateX(-100%) -> translateX(460%) over 900ms steps(2, end) infinite
motion.purpose: The loader's advancing frame line; replaced by a static 40%-opacity rule under reduced motion.

layout.name: strip
layout.purpose: Top strip height; redeclared in the token layer so the wrap costs one line.

layout.name: rail
layout.purpose: Index column width and drawer width.

layout.name: frame-min
layout.purpose: Intrinsic grid track floor; column count has no breakpoint.

components.css: .ds-loader { width: 100%; min-height: 2px; margin: 32px 0; background: var(--rule, #454e55); overflow: hidden; } .ds-loader::after { content: ''; display: block; width: 28%; height: 2px; background: var(--mark, #ff4a14); animation: ds-advance 900ms steps(2, end) infinite; } @keyframes ds-advance { from { transform: translateX(-100%); } to { transform: translateX(460%); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-loader::after { animation: none; width: 100%; opacity: 0.4; } }

narrative.overview:
This is a film archive's own material: the vault dark, the backlit light table, the grease pencil. The catalogue is not a storefront of cards — it is one continuous ruled strip of frames on a sheet, each with its accession code and year written in the gutter beneath it. Nothing floats, nothing lifts, nothing rounds. The only hue in the entire interface is the grease pencil; every other value is a cool achromatic neutral, so the poster artwork is the only other colour the page paints.

Density and legibility outrank decoration. The chrome is hairlines and mono labels; the content is the posters. The system is deliberately built out of platform features rather than dependencies — system type stacks, light-dark(), intrinsic grid, content-visibility — because weight is spent against the argument this app exists to make. Every token is declared once; a value that appears twice is a token that is missing.

The test the world has to pass is the empty-frames test: with every poster removed, the field still has to read as a ruled grid of frames with codes in the gutters. It does — that is what the hairline rules and the gutter mono are for, and it is why the frames carry their own rules rather than relying on a grid gap.
keyCharacteristics: One chromatic hue in the whole system; everything else achromatic and cool.
Zero border-radius and zero box-shadow, anywhere, without exception.
Rank is ply — which sheet a thing sits on — plus a 1px hairline.
A grotesk/mono split where the mono carries codes, years, figures and labels, never prose.
Two-frame step motion at 90ms with no easing curve anywhere.
Column count is intrinsic; the responsive system has exactly two breakpoint values.

rules.name: The One Hue Rule
rules.body: --mark is the only non-achromatic token in the system. If a new surface needs a second colour, it needs a reason that outranks the law — and it will not find one, because poster artwork is the colour. Audit test: grep the stylesheets for a literal colour; everything that is not --mark must be grey.

rules.name: The Two Rules Rule
rules.body: A hairline is either structure (--rule) or a control boundary (--rule-strong). Structure may sit under 3:1 because nothing is read from it; anything that bounds something clickable takes --rule-strong and clears 3:1 on every ply.

rules.name: The Faint-Is-Text Rule
rules.body: --ink-faint is used for small mono labels people actually read, so it is held to 4.5:1 against every ply in both themes — not to the 3:1 bar its visual weight suggests.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: The mono face carries accession codes, years, figures, counts and short uppercase labels — never body copy, never a heading, never a sentence. If it would be read as prose, it is set in the grotesk.

rules.name: The No-Webfont Rule
rules.body: No @font-face, no font CDN, no icon font. The type ramp is fluid clamp() with no html { font-size } hack and no breakpoint ladder, so size is continuous across every viewport.

rules.name: The Intrinsic Column Rule
rules.body: Column count is never set by a breakpoint. New grids use auto-fill over a fluid minmax() track; if a layout seems to need a third breakpoint, it needs an intrinsic track instead.

rules.name: The One Markup Rule
rules.body: The same DOM serves phone and desktop. A responsive change is a CSS rule, never a branch — this keeps the SSR payload identical for every device, which is what makes hydration at the edge correct.

rules.name: The Two Breakpoints Rule
rules.body: 48rem (the strip returns to one row; page padding and the detail card go two-column) and 64rem (the index sits beside the field). Adding a third breakpoint value is a system change, not a local fix.

rules.name: The Ply Rule
rules.body: A thing is never above another thing; it is on a ply. Rank is expressed by moving to the next ply and drawing a hairline. A new surface that reaches for a shadow is asking for a ply it has not been given.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: box-shadow is not used for elevation, for hover, for focus, or for glow. Focus is a ring and a drawn mark; hover is a ply change.

dos: Do take every colour from the token layer, and declare both themes in a single light-dark() pair at the point the token is defined.
Do carry rank with a ply change plus a hairline (--ply-0 → --ply-1 → --ply-2).
Do use --rule for structure and --rule-strong for anything that bounds a control.
Do set codes, years, figures and short uppercase labels in the mono stack with tabular-nums, and prose in the grotesk.
Do express every responsive change in CSS — intrinsic grid first, then one of the two existing breakpoints.
Do animate with var(--step) var(--step-fn) (90ms, steps(2, end)) and nothing else.

Do release content-visibility to visible on the hovered or focused frame. The frame carries content-visibility: auto for off-screen work, and that applies paint containment which clips the chinagraph's overhang; releasing it only on interaction keeps the saving where it actually pays, since the interacted frame is on screen by definition.

Do recolour injected brand SVGs globally by id (#movies-logo .st0, #tmdb-logo .cls-1) and apply transforms to the <fast-svg> host, never to the inner <svg>. The injected SVG lives in that component's own view and carries no encapsulation attribute from the parent, so a parent's scoped descendant selector cannot reach it.
Do keep TMDB attribution visible, linked, and at a legible ink in both themes.
Do reach for a platform feature before a dependency, and a token before a one-off.
donts: Don't introduce a second chromatic hue. Poster artwork is the colour.
Don't use box-shadow — not for elevation, hover, focus or glow.
Don't use a non-zero border-radius anywhere.
Don't add an easing curve. There is no cubic-bezier, ease-in or ease-out in this project and the step function is the grammar, not a default.
Don't add a webfont, an icon font, a CSS framework or a UI component library. Bundle size is a product constraint and every one of these spends it.
Don't branch on viewport size in TypeScript or in a template, and don't add a JavaScript media-query listener. It breaks SSR/hydration parity at the edge.
Don't make magnitude iconic — no star rows, no filled/empty glyph repeats.
Don't let the chinagraph mark be the sole focus indicator on any surface where it is drawn over uncontrolled imagery; pair it with the two-tone ring.
Don't separate frames with a grid gap. The strip is continuous; the frames draw their own rules.
Don't put a short invented word above a heading as a kicker or eyebrow. The accession label beside a page title is for real catalogue data (a tagline, a year, a source count).
